data.description:
Goal:
After K-58 added `thimble exec` and a Consuming Secrets section, several
docs still framed `render → file` as the canonical flow. Realign every
operator-facing doc around the secure-by-default happy path and ship
language-tabbed code samples for receiving the dotenv body in apps.

Verification:
1. README has a top-level "Quickstart — the secure happy path" section
   placed right after Install, walking the operator from `age-keygen`
   through `thimble exec` end-to-end with no plaintext on disk.
2. README "Consuming Secrets From Your App" section has language-
   tabbed code samples (collapsible <details>) for Python, TypeScript,
   Go, Rust — replacing the older sequential Go/Python/Node.js block.
3. README "Real-Life Flow" is reduced to an ASCII topology + pointer
   to Quickstart, removing the duplicate plaintext-render walkthrough.
4. README "Consuming Secrets" preface notes that helper libraries
   (thimble-py/ts/go/rust) are planned (links to K-60..K-63 trackers).
5. scripts/demo.sh extended with `verify`, `exec`, and `audit` steps;
   the exec step pipes the dotenv body to a child that prints key
   names + value lengths only, demonstrating the no-leak property.
6. Demo cast/gif refreshed (operator action — re-record locally).

Constraints:
- Knot ref: K-59; follow-ups: K-60/K-61/K-62/K-63 (helper libs).
- No code changes outside scripts/demo.sh and the README.
- Tab UI uses GitHub-native <details><summary> collapsibles; no JS, no
  external docs site.
- The four code samples must be self-contained, runnable as-is, and use
  only the standard library of each language. No `python-dotenv` etc.
- The "helper libraries are planned" note must not link to external
  third-party vault products (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, etc.).
- Demo script must remain <50 lines of new content over the prior
  version; receiver script must NOT print values.
